answer: PUF-anchored deployment passports: each identity requires a fresh SRAM-PUF fingerprint, a signed beacon receipt from its assigned atlas cell, and continuous low-latency probes from that site; island and inlet cells use distinct beacon keys. A single operator cannot clone one chip’s silicon fingerprint into many identities or simulate multiple site paths without separate hardware and network presence. Attacker cost: one distinct PUF device plus site-specific beacon/network maintenance per sybil.
